question: What recoverable contract should the public `socket.drain` event provide when a subscribed WebSocket is slow: bounded queue with disconnect/reconnect, ordinary best-effort delivery, or another documented mechanism?
rationale: The requested feature is a newly advertised gateway event, and neither an unbounded existing event stream nor silently dropped teardown telemetry defines a safe durable client contract.

options.title: Adopt bounded delivery
options.body: Keep ordinary `sessions.changed` backpressure and make slow `socket.drain` subscribers recover through a bounded queue plus explicit connection close/reconnect semantics.

options.title: Use best-effort delivery
options.body: Retain normal drop behavior for `socket.drain` and document that clients must reconcile state after reconnecting or polling.

options.title: Defer the public event
options.body: Pause this feature until maintainers select and document the WebSocket recovery semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded delivery
recommendation.body: Keep ordinary `sessions.changed` backpressure and make slow `socket.drain` subscribers recover through a bounded queue plus explicit connection close/reconnect semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch author can supply the implementation and exact-head evidence, while final protocol acceptance remains a repository maintainer decision.
